result.note: Tests the BNP victory and Tarique Rahman's background, and the location of the China-backed Teesta project near the Siliguri Corridor.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the Bangladesh general election held in February 2026:
items: The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) defeated an 11-party Islamist alliance in the first elections held since the 2024 uprising.
BNP leader Tarique Rahman is the son of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.
Dhaka is seeking Sheikh Hasina's extradition from India for crimes against humanity.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because Tarique Rahman is the son of the late former Prime Minister Khaleda Zia, and he returned after 17 years in self-exile. Hasina's extradition remains a sore point because New Delhi is still sheltering her.
questions.source: Leader Tarique Rahman – son of the late former Prime Minister Khaleda Zia – now inherits a fractured nation after 17 years in self-exile.

questions.prompt: In February 2026, the new BNP government's interest in a China-backed river project near India's Siliguri Corridor was seen as a source of friction with New Delhi. Which river is this project on?
questions.explain: The BNP has shown interest in the China-backed Teesta River project near the sensitive Siliguri Corridor. TBB's analysis notes that New Delhi is trying to keep Dhaka from pivoting fully into China's orbit.
questions.source: Add to this the BNP’s interest in the China-backed Teesta River project near the sensitive Siliguri Corridor, and the reset looks increasingly uphill.
